_comment: Accepted Semgrep findings (contrib/semgrep/README.md, 'Fixing or accepting a finding'). findings: fingerprint -> {rule, path, reason, by, date}. rule_paths: [{rule (glob), paths (globs), reason, by, date}]. Every entry needs a reason a reviewer can check.

78181d7454a9c410.reason: GET / is the merchant's free index: it lists the paid routes and whether each is wired, and serves no paid resource. Every paid handler is registered after app.use(paymentMiddleware(...)) (app.ts, the handlers loop).

a2f5dddc3f04a10c.reason: Builds the vendored Falcon C with the C compiler the operator chose ($CC, as every C build honours); an argv list, no shell, the other arguments are this package's own source paths and a mkstemp name.

7294fdf75dd9b22f.reason: Same call as a2f5dddc3f04a10c: the compiler invocation, an argv list without a shell.

64a96d48adf6c40b.reason: serde_json::to_value of the crate's own plain structs (no maps with non-string keys, no custom Serialize) cannot fail.

99d23aeb9b5c6040.reason: Response::builder with a constant status and header cannot fail; the body is the reply already built.

eb3344d78458358c.reason: The transaction was built a few lines earlier with a Sapling bundle (the only kind light/ builds); the expect states that invariant.

801c0ab7e8dbfd4b.reason: scan_chunk indexes blocks[0] first, and its caller passes only non-empty chunks; blocks.last() is Some.

426b4c292e33cb1f.reason: Same invariant as 801c0ab7e8dbfd4b: a chunk is never empty.

rule_paths.reason: sqlite3, not SQLAlchemy: every value is a ? parameter; the f-strings only splice the class constant _LIVE and a run of '?' placeholders.

The vendored PQClean falcon-padded-512 code (from the node's src/crypto/pq/falcon): the memsets zero algorithm state (keygen) and signature padding (ycash_falcon_sign.c), not secrets to wipe; kept byte-for-byte with the node copy.
Local measurement tools (tools/x4m, run by hand against the operator's own node) and devnet tests: subprocess argv lists and urllib to a URL the operator passes; no shell, no untrusted input.
Picks which mainnet blocks to sample for a size measurement (tools/x4m/mainnet_block_sizes.py); nothing secret.
Command-line measurement tools: argv is the operator's own input.
#[cfg(test)] fake lightwalletd: a scratch directory for a unit test.
Test code (#[cfg(test)] fake lightwalletd, the regtest integration test): a panic is a failed test.
A devnet test's console.warn text containing "<tip + 100 or more>"; nothing is rendered as HTML.
Test vectors, regtest keys and documentation examples, not real secrets. A secret anywhere else is still reported.
